expectations.text: States loop body tasks must not transition to error handlers outside the loop
expectations.evidence: No statement anywhere in the transcript or in the produced workflow JSON addresses transitioning loop-body tasks to error handlers outside the loop. The transcript's three answers only cover job_id/incoming, cross-loop $var resolution, and the empty-transition rule for the last body task; error-handling routing for loop-body tasks is never discussed. The produced JSON's loop-body evaluation task (3c4d) has only success/failure transitions to other in-loop tasks (5e6f/7a8b) and no error transition at all, so the artifact neither demonstrates nor discusses this rule. A grep of the skill file for 'loop.*error'/'error.*loop'/'outside the loop' plus 'error handler' turned up no documented rule of this shape either, so it's unclear this expectation is even grounded in the skill's content.

suggestions.assertion: States loop body tasks must not transition to error handlers outside the loop
suggestions.reason: This expectation doesn't correspond to anything in the three questions actually posed in the task prompt (job_id, cross-loop $var reference, last-task transition), and a targeted grep of the skill file for loop/error-handler language found no documented rule of this exact shape. If this is a real platform gotcha the skill should teach, it may be missing from SKILL.md entirely (a skill gap worth flagging to the skill author) rather than an eval that the executor failed to apply; if it's not actually a documented or true rule, the assertion should be revised or removed since no executor could satisfy it without inventing content not in the skill.

Interestingly, the real production asset (itential-platform-configuration-management.json, 'Backup Configuration' workflow) has a loop-body task (a6d5) with an error transition to another in-chain evaluation task (822c) that itself transitions out on failure — this is a real example of loop-body error routing behavior that neither the transcript nor the produced illustrative JSON examines or discusses, despite the transcript explicitly pulling from this same asset file for other purposes. A stronger eval might explicitly ask the executor to trace what happens on error inside the loop body, since the current three questions don't probe that path at all, leaving expectation 4 essentially untestable by the given prompt.

eval_feedback.overall: Three of four expectations are well-supported with high-quality, verifiable evidence — the executor did not just repeat the skill's language but cross-checked it against a real production asset export (grep+jq) and produced an illustrative workflow JSON that structurally embodies each answer (data_array-only incoming, job-variable-bound evaluation output, empty terminal transitions). The one failing expectation (error handlers outside the loop) appears disconnected both from the original task prompt's three questions and from any rule discoverable in the skill file itself, so it may be an eval assertion that needs re-grounding rather than a genuine executor miss.
